newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt disagrees with Israel on Palestinian state.
newsitem.headline: Egypt disagrees with Israel on Palestinian state.

text.p: Egypt disagreed openly with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday over the possibility of a Palestinian state, saying such a state was an essential ingredient in Middle East peace.

Foreign Minister Amr Moussa, after briefing President Hosni Mubarak on his trip to France and Norway this week, told reporters: "Egypt believes that setting up a Palestinian state alone is the real guarantee of a real peace. "To deny, ignore
or resist the Palestinian people's right to have their own state and to practice their right to self-determination is a denial of the whole essence of peace."
He was commenting on Netanyahu's remarks this week saying he would never allow a Palestinian state alongside Israel.

Moussa said Egypt also opposed any renegotiation of the old agreement on Israeli redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron, the most urgent issue in negotiations between Israel and the Palestinians.

"If the negotiations are reopened, it would not be a step forward...Egypt's position is clear -- to implement the agreements, build on them and act according to the Madrid formula of land for peace and the Oslo framework," he said.
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat is expected in Cairo shortly to brief Mubarak on his first talks with Netanyahu.
